title: Neural Marked Point Processes for Health Insurance Claims
abstract: arXiv:2611.21326v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Health insurance claims exhibit temporal dependence, as previous claims may provide information about the timing, type and amount of subsequent claims. Such dependencies are difficult to capture with traditional actuarial models based on aggregated claim counts. We investigate a neural marked point process in which a causal Transformer represents individual claim histories and determines type-specific conditional intensities, allowing for self-excitation and interactions between claim types. The framework also incorporates conditional severity distributions, reporting delays and stochastic medical-cost inflation. We develop a likelihood-based calibration procedure that accounts for incomplete claim reporting and evaluate the model using both simulated and empirical data.
